title: A hostile is now findable in the frame the game actually makes, while the screen is red — and the gate reads that frame, not a bench

verified.THE ABLATION, on the ordinary output of: artifacts/H1_v1 is a full first_night visual run of THE TREATMENT AS IT SHIPPED with only the new instrument added. tests/render/run_foe_frame.gd against it: lift 0/9, cold 6/9, blind scan lands on 1 of 6 packs — 3 of 6 checks RED. Against artifacts/H1_v5 (the fix): lift 9/9, cold 9/9, blind 6 of 6 packs — GREEN. Reproduced independently in artifacts/H1_final: 9/9, 9/9, 6 of 6, camera offset +16,-8.
verified.delivered contrast on shots/assault.worl: the nine hostiles measure 0.021-0.146 luminance above the plain before, 0.18-0.34 after. The gate's bar is 0.17, chosen to sit in the gap between the two populations, and it never moved during tuning.
verified.friend/foe hue in the same file: blue-minus-red above the surrounding plain went 6/9 above +0.030 to 9/9. Three hostiles previously read WARMER than the ground they stood on, i.e. indistinguishable from a citizen.
verified.why the previous fix could not be seen (: ground_luma reads 0.502, 0.680, 0.678, 0.367 under the hostiles that were inside the perimeter, because they stand in the city's firelight. Against GROUND_PIVOT 0.34 that is lit_share 0.05/0.00/0.00/0.49 — the treatment switched itself OFF for exactly the creatures the alert stack was shouting about. The same pixels measure ~0.10 in the photograph. The hostile treatment is now keyed to light_energy (the hour) instead.
verified.A REAL BUG, found by photographing it: RendererCanvasCull::canvas_item_add_texture_rect_region turns a negative destination width into a flip flag by negating rect.size.x and LEAVING rect.position. Every right-facing figure in this game — enemies and citizens — was drawn ONE FULL SPRITE WIDTH (41 screen px at play zoom) to the right of the tile the simulation had it on. Caught by putting a light pool at ag["pos"] and finding four hounds 50 px to the right of their own light in artifacts/H1_smoke/shots/night_perimeter.world.png. Now flips the SOURCE region; shadow, pool, boot marks and sim position agree.
verified.occlusion: [P03]'s belt overlay is z 1 and its machine plates z 4, both above the figures. In artifacts/H1_v3 a hound standing on a conveyor measured lift 0.033 where its neighbours measured 0.30. A hostile now gets one additive cold quad at z 5; that creature is 0.18 in artifacts/H1_final.
verified.the gate's own control: the same blind scan on a night frame from the same run with ZERO hostiles alive — 35/38 clusters before the fix, 39/40 after. The interface is what a blind cold-bright scan mostly finds (this is what produced the critic's '105 pixels, both temperature labels'), so the noise budget is measured off that control rather than declared as a constant.
verified.the camera moves between the log line an: every hostile in artifacts/H1_v5 landed +18,-10 from its logged rectangle, the SAME offset for all nine. The gate aligns the frame ONCE, globally, on two parameters, and prints the offset. A single shared translation cannot move nine dark rectangles onto nine bright things that are not there.
verified.tests/render/night_contrast.tscn, tests/: TESTS PASSED, PARTIAL (unchanged — both are PARTIAL headless on this box)
verified.engine errors in the visual run: 0 blocking, 0 benign, 1 known (resources still in use at exit); 0 [ERROR] lines in artifacts/H1_v5/log.txt
verified.the 'under attack' feel was not spent: corner redness (r-b) on assault.world.png is 0.0779 before and 0.0783 after — the threat vignette is exactly as loud in the margin where it lives. It stopped reaching into the playfield: mid-edge 0.0725 -> 0.0677, playfield unchanged.
verified.sim untouched: the whole change is game/view/render/entity_renderer.gd, game/view/feel/screen_fx.gd and tests/render/run_foe_frame.gd. Nothing under game/sim/**.

open: render_perf.tscn is RED at collect 3578 us against a 3000 us budget — but it is red at 3523 us on the PARENT COMMIT too (A/B'd by checking 0e212fc's entity_renderer.gd into a scratch and re-running on a quiet box). This is a pre-existing budget failure on this hardware, not a regression; my change moved it 1.6%. Some of that 1.6% is bookkeeping: the visible-agent collection moved OUT of the draw pass and INTO _collect, which removed a duplicate model.agents(alpha) call per frame but re-attributed the remainder to a stage the headless budget actually measures. INTEGRATOR must re-measure alone.

tools/determinism.sh was NOT run: another agent is actively editing game/sim/logistics/** in this working tree, so a replay would be grading their in-flight change, not mine. My diff touches no file under game/sim/.

tools/check.sh's visual stage runs --scenario=smoke, which has no night frame with ZERO hostiles in it, so run_foe_frame.gd reports its control UNCHECKED there and the verdict is PARTIAL rather than green. The clean fix is one line of tools/gate.sh (which I do not own): either run first_night, or add a 0-hostile night beat to tests/scenarios/smoke.json. Until then, run it against a first_night run: LCN_FRAME_DIR=artifacts/<run> godot --headless --path . --script tests/render/run_foe_frame.gd

[P03]: the belt overlay (z 1), item layer (z 3) and machine plates (z 4) all draw ABOVE agents, so a creature or a citizen standing on a conveyor is cut in half by it. I worked around it for hostiles with an additive halo at z 5; citizens are still sliced. The right fix is on their side of the fence.

The foe treatment is hostile-only and night-only by design (light_energy 1.30 at night, 0.14 at midday, so _dark_share is 1.0 and 0.0). A DAY assault gets the old silhouette treatment and has never been photographed — no scenario in tests/scenarios/ stages one.

Tuning headroom is bounded by packs, not by singles: four hounds standing on each other stack four additive pools and read as one bright mass (artifacts/H1_smoke4 shows it at FOE_HALO_A 0.32). FOE_HALO_A is at 0.26 for that reason. If someone wants louder singles, the pool needs to be drawn once per CLUSTER rather than once per creature.
